sam_support: Heads-up: customer (acct: acme-media) seeing intermittent SSE 401 mid-stream. Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d. Happened ~3x in last 24h, last at 2025-11-12T14:20Z. Need a minimal curl repro that includes the auth headers + proxy chain info so we can validate handshake. @lee_eng @ben_eng_runtime can you assist? I'll collect a debug bundle.

lee_eng: Can you paste the raw response headers from the failing attempt (we need the exact x-request-id and any x-auth-reason)? Also whether they use HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 through the proxy.

sam_support: Pasted from customer logs: ```HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d
x-auth-reason: token_expired
date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 14:20:11 GMT
content-length: 24
``` They also sent a client-side trace: "EOF while waiting for server" and proxy shows `upstream reset`. Customer says proxy = charter-proxy v2.1, keepalive enabled.

maya_support: They also reported that preceding the 401 there was a ~700ms hop in latency for several minutes. Could be rotation TTL or proxy re-use issue.

ben_eng_runtime: Likely token rotation hit while connection reused. Quick experiments to try: 1) reproduce streaming with a long-running curl (-N) and force connection reuse (keepalive) 2) reproduce with Connection: close (no reuse). Example minimal repro I used in staging:```bash
# streaming with keepalive (may reproduce)
curl -v -N \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d" \ 
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-medium&stream=true'

# streaming with no keepalive (control)
curl -v -N -H "Connection: close" -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_WITH_TOKEN" 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-medium&stream=true'
```
Try both and capture `--trace-ascii debug.txt`.

alex_support: I validated a variant in staging that included proxy headers and http1.1:```bash
curl -v -N --http1.1 \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 54.12.34.56" \ 
  -H "X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d" \ 
  --proxy http://charter-proxy:3128 \ 
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-medium&stream=true'
```
That reproduces a clean stream for ~10m in staging. To provoke the issue, you can rotate the token with a TTL ~60s and keep the curl alive longer.

opssre_bot: incident created: INCIDENT-1423 for r-0a1b2c3d (auto).

ben_eng_runtime: If you can reproduce locally, please attach the `--trace-ascii` output plus the exact `curl -v` stderr. On server side, we'll correlate `x-request-id` with our trace logs and kernel-level socket resets. If proxy is in the path, get proxy logs (CONNECT, keepalive reuse).

lee_eng: Also try `--raw` and `--no-buffer` variants to ensure there isn't client buffering confusion. If you get a 401, capture TCP-level timing: from `curl --trace-time`. That helps show whether token expiry coincides with last successful chunk.

carol_billing: FYI I noticed a billing spike reported around the same timestamps for that customer — might be unrelated but attaching billing trace could help rule out duplicate retries counting as extra tokens.

sam_support: Plan: 1) I'll ask customer to run the two curl variants above and include `--trace-ascii debug.txt` + `--trace-time` + `--verbose` output, and to export proxy CONNECT logs for the same window. 2) If they reproduce, they'll upload bundle to our secure bucket and I'll paste link here. 3) @ben_eng_runtime and @lee_eng will correlate server traces for r-0a1b2c3d and check token-rotation logs.

sam_support: Quick checklist I'm sending to customer (short):
- Replace TOKEN with current bearer token used by client.
- Run both: keepalive and Connection: close.
- Use `--trace-ascii debug.txt --trace-time -v` and attach debug.txt.
- Provide proxy logs for same interval and client library name/version.
- Note exact local clock time (UTC) when you saw 401.

lee_eng: Sounds good. If they can't run curl, request a packet capture (pcap) of the TLS handshake and the moment of the 401 — we'll scrub before uploading.

sam_support: Thanks all — I'll follow up when bundle is in. :mag:
